examples.ko: 급한 일이 생겨서 월급을 가불 받았어요.
examples.en: Something urgent came up, so I got an advance on my salary.
It was urgent, so I asked the boss for an advance.

examples.ko: 이번 달 월급은 가불 때문에 많이 줄었어요.
examples.en: This month's pay is much smaller because of the advance.
I asked the HR team whether an advance is possible.

examples.ko: 가불로 받은 돈은 다음 달 월급에서 빼요.
examples.en: The money received as an advance is deducted from next month's pay.
Where do I fill out the advance request form?

explain: 월급날 전에 일부를 미리 받는 것을 말해요. 받는 사람은 '가불을 받다', 주는 쪽은 '가불을 해 주다'라고 말해요. 나중에 월급에서 빼는 돈이라서 그냥 '빌리다'와는 느낌이 달라요.

phrases.en: I got an advance on my pay this month.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일하는 사람이 월급을 미리 받을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used by the worker who receives pay early.

phrases.en: My boss gave me an advance.
phrases.nuance_ko: 주는 쪽에서 하는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Said from the side of the person who gives it.

phrases.en: Is a salary advance possible?
phrases.nuance_ko: 회사에 물어볼 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used when asking your company.

explain_en: It means receiving part of your pay before payday. The person receiving says '가불을 받다', and the side giving it says '가불을 해 주다'. Since it is deducted from later pay, it feels different from simply borrowing money.

examples.en: I got my salary in advance from the company.
I needed money urgently, so I decided to take an advance.

examples.ko: 이번 달 월급을 가불하면 다음 달이 힘들어요.
examples.en: If I take this month's pay in advance, next month will be hard.

examples.ko: 사장님이 가불해 주셔서 월세를 낼 수 있었어요.
examples.en: The boss gave me an advance, so I could pay the rent.
If you want an advance, tell the manager first.

examples.ko: 한 번 가불한 돈은 꼭 갚아야 해요.
examples.en: Money you have once taken as an advance must be paid back.

explain: 일하는 사람이 월급을 미리 받을 때는 '가불하다', 회사나 사장님이 미리 줄 때는 '가불해 주다'라고 말해요. 짝말로 '월급을 가불하다'가 자주 나와요. 일상에서는 '가불 받다'라고도 많이 말해요.

phrases.en: My boss paid my salary in advance.
phrases.nuance_ko: 주는 쪽이 주어일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the giver is the subject.

phrases.en: It was urgent, so I got an advance.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서 '가불하다'만큼 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: As common in daily speech as 'gabulhada'.

phrases.en: I'd like to get a little of my salary in advance.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부탁할 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when making a request.

explain_en: A worker getting pay early says '가불하다', and when the company or boss gives it early they say '가불해 주다'. A common pairing is '월급을 가불하다'. In daily talk people also often say '가불 받다'.

en: to slash one's pay; to cut one's pay

examples.ko: 회사는 규칙을 어긴 직원의 월급을 감봉하기로 했어요.
examples.en: The company decided to cut the pay of the employee who broke the rules.

examples.ko: 사장님이 한 달 동안 월급을 감봉한다고 발표했어요.
examples.en: The boss announced that salaries would be cut for a month.

examples.ko: 잘못이 커서 석 달 감봉했다고 들었어요.
examples.en: I heard they cut his pay for three months because the mistake was serious.
If you cut salaries, employees' complaints grow.

examples.ko: 회사 사정이 어렵다고 월급을 감봉하는 건 문제예요.
examples.en: Cutting pay just because the company is struggling is a problem.
He complained that even with his pay cut, it's hard to reduce living expenses.

explain: 주로 잘못에 대한 징계로 일정 기간 월급을 깎을 때 써요. 그냥 돈을 줄이는 '삭감하다'나 구어체 '깎다'와 달리 사람의 월급에 쓰고, '감봉 처분'이라는 말로 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: That employee received a pay cut as discipline.
phrases.nuance_ko: 징계로 월급을 깎는 결정을 말하는 가장 흔한 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing for a disciplinary pay cut.

phrases.example: 실수 때문에 석 달 동안 감봉됐어요.
phrases.en: I had my pay cut for three months because of a mistake.
phrases.nuance_ko: 월급이 깎인 사람 입장에서 말하는 피동 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A passive form from the point of view of the person whose pay is cut.

phrases.en: The company cut a month of pay.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말할 때 쓰는 쉬운 표현이고, '감봉하다'보다 덜 딱딱해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A plain spoken expression, less formal than 감봉하다.

explain_en: It is mainly used when pay is cut for a set period as a disciplinary measure. Unlike '삭감하다' (to cut an amount) or the casual '깎다', it applies to a person's salary, and it often appears in the phrase '감봉 처분' (a pay-cut penalty).

examples.en: I received a generous bonus, so I'm in a good mood.

examples.ko: 날씨가 추우니까 옷을 두둑이 껴입고 나가세요.
examples.en: It's cold, so bundle up thickly before you go out.

examples.ko: 할머니는 손님에게 음식을 두둑이 싸 주셨어요.
examples.en: Grandma packed plenty of food for the guest.
Business went well and I made a good amount of money.

examples.ko: 시험 전에 밥을 두둑이 먹고 갔어요.
examples.en: I ate a hearty meal before the exam and went.
Thank you for giving me such generous pocket money.

explain: 두껍고 넉넉하다는 느낌으로, 돈·음식·옷처럼 양이 충분할 때 써요. 형용사 '두둑하다'(지갑이 두둑하다)와 함께 알아 두면 좋아요.

phrases.en: It's payday, so my wallet is full.
phrases.nuance_ko: 형용사 '두둑하다'로 바꿔 쓰면 상태를 말할 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: The adjective form 두둑하다 describes a state.

phrases.example: 여행 가기 전에 용돈을 두둑이 챙겼어요.
phrases.en: Before the trip, I packed plenty of spending money.
phrases.nuance_ko: 돈이나 짐을 넉넉하게 준비할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you prepare money or things generously.

phrases.en: My grandfather gave me a generous New Year's gift of money.
phrases.nuance_ko: 돈을 넉넉하게 줄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when giving money generously.

explain_en: It conveys a thick, ample feeling and is used when there is plenty of something, like money, food or clothing. It is useful to learn it together with the adjective '두둑하다' (as in '지갑이 두둑하다').

examples.en: It's payday, so my wallet is full.
I slept under a thick, well-stuffed cotton quilt.
I received a generous bonus.
Dad's pocket was always full of allowance money.
I feel good looking at my fattened bank account.
The winter jacket is thickly padded, so it's warm to wear.

explain: 돈이 넉넉할 때 '지갑이 두둑하다', '용돈을 두둑이 주다'처럼 써요. 옷이나 이불이 두껍고 속이 꽉 찬 것에도 쓰지만 요즘 대화에서는 돈 이야기에서 더 많이 나와요.

phrases.en: have plenty of money
phrases.nuance_ko: 실제 주머니가 아니라 돈이 넉넉하다는 뜻으로 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Not about an actual pocket; it means one has plenty of money.

explain_en: It is used for plenty of money: '지갑이 두둑하다', '용돈을 두둑이 주다'. It also fits thick, well-padded clothes and quilts, but these days it comes up mostly in talk about money.

examples.en: Despite the low pay, he likes his job.
A new hire's salary is so low that life is tight.

examples.ko: 박봉으로 아이 셋을 키우기가 쉽지 않아요.
examples.en: It isn't easy to raise three kids on a low salary.
My father struggled with low pay all his life.

examples.ko: 박봉이지만 보람 있는 일이라서 계속 다녀요.
examples.en: The pay is low, but the work is rewarding, so I keep going.

examples.ko: 박봉을 받는 사람들을 위한 지원이 필요해요.
examples.en: Support is needed for people who receive low pay.

explain: 월급이 적다는 뜻을 한 단어로 말하는 표현이에요. '박봉에 시달리다', '박봉이다'처럼 쓰고, 반대는 '고액 연봉'이에요. 구어로는 '월급이 짜다'라고도 해요.

phrases.en: He suffered from a poor salary for a long time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 월급이 적어서 힘든 상황을 말할 때 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common phrase for struggling because of low pay.

phrases.en: This job pays little, but it's rewarding.
phrases.nuance_ko: 서술어로 써서 '월급이 적다'는 뜻을 한 번에 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used as a predicate to say 'the pay is low' in one word.

phrases.en: My company pays a stingy salary.
phrases.nuance_ko: '박봉'과 같은 뜻의 구어체로, 친구와 편하게 말할 때 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: A colloquial equivalent of '박봉', suited to casual talk with friends.

explain_en: It packs 'the salary is small' into one word. It is used as '박봉에 시달리다' or '박봉이다', and the opposite is '고액 연봉' (a high annual salary). In casual speech people also say '월급이 짜다'.

en: house for an employee; employee residence

examples.ko: 회사에서 사택을 빌려 줘서 월세 부담이 적어요.
examples.en: The company lends me housing, so the rent burden is small.

examples.ko: 이 공장 직원들은 대부분 사택에서 살아요.
examples.en: Most of the employees at this factory live in company housing.
The company housing is close to work, so commuting is easy.
I have to leave the company housing when I quit, so I'm worried.

examples.ko: 사택 단지에는 직원 가족들이 많이 살아요.
examples.en: Many employees' families live in the company housing complex.
We moved into the company housing of the firm where my father worked.

explain: 회사가 직원에게 빌려주는 집이에요. 공무원이나 교사, 군인 같은 사람에게 기관이 주는 집은 보통 '관사'라고 해요. 미혼 직원이 함께 지내는 곳은 '기숙사'라고 불러요.

phrases.en: I live in company housing, so commuting is easy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 회사가 주는 집에 산다고 말할 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A collocation for living in housing provided by the company.

phrases.en: This company provides housing for its employees.
phrases.nuance_ko: 회사가 직원에게 집을 준다는 뜻으로 구인 글에 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means a company gives employees housing, often seen in job postings.

phrases.en: The teacher stays in official housing provided by the school.
phrases.nuance_ko: 회사가 아니라 공공 기관이 공무원, 교사 등에게 주는 집이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Housing given by a public institution to officials or teachers, not by a company.

explain_en: It is a home a company provides to its employees. A home provided by an institution to civil servants, teachers or soldiers is usually called '관사'. A place where single employees stay together is called '기숙사' (dormitory).

en: to be deposited; to be put into a bank account

examples.en: Half of my salary is automatically put into my savings account.

examples.ko: 아껴 둔 돈이 어제 통장에 예금됐어요.
examples.en: The money I saved up was put into my account yesterday.
The New Year gift money will be put into the child's account.

examples.ko: 통장에 예금되는 돈이 조금씩 늘고 있어요.
examples.en: The amount being deposited into my account is slowly growing.
After the money was deposited, a text message came.
A lump sum has been put into my account, so I feel at ease.

explain: 사람이 돈을 은행에 맡기면 '예금하다', 그 돈이 통장에 들어가 쌓이면 '예금되다'로 말해요. 돈이 들어온 것만 말할 때는 '입금되다'가 더 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: When I get paid, I deposit money in the bank.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이 돈을 맡기는 행동을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the person's act of depositing money.

phrases.en: My salary was deposited into my account today.
phrases.nuance_ko: 돈이 들어온 사실만 말할 때 더 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: More natural when you only state that money came in.

phrases.en: I opened a new savings account book.
phrases.nuance_ko: 돈을 모으는 통장을 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to an account book for saving money.

explain_en: When a person leaves money at a bank, it is 예금하다, and when that money goes into the account and builds up, it is 예금되다. If you only mean that money arrived, 입금되다 is more natural.

en: to be badly off; to be needy

examples.en: My salary is small, so we're badly off.

examples.ko: 방이 옹색해서 짐을 둘 곳이 없어요.
examples.en: The room is so cramped that there's no place for my things.
Even as an excuse, that's really lame.
Even in a cramped house, the family lived laughing.

examples.ko: 돈 때문에 옹색하게 사는 게 싫어요.
examples.en: I hate living on a tight budget because of money.

examples.ko: 사정이 옹색해도 아이 교육만큼은 포기하지 않았어요.
examples.en: Even though we were hard up, we didn't give up on our child's education.

explain: 돈이 없어서 형편이 어렵거나 공간이 좁아서 답답할 때 써요. '변명이 옹색하다'처럼 말이 궁색할 때도 쓰는데, '궁색하다'와 비슷해요.

phrases.example: 옹색한 살림에도 우리 가족은 웃으며 살아요.
phrases.en: Even though our household is badly off, our family lives with smiles.
phrases.nuance_ko: 표제어를 뒤의 말을 꾸미는 형태로 바꿔, 돈이 부족한 생활을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form of the headword, used for a life lacking money.

phrases.example: 새로 이사한 집은 옹색하지 않고 넉넉해요.
phrases.en: The house we moved to isn't cramped; it's roomy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형으로 쓰면 공간이나 형편이 좁거나 어렵지 않다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form means the space or situation is not cramped or hard.

phrases.en: That person's excuse is really lame.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비슷한 뜻의 말로, 형편이 어렵거나 말이 부족할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A similar word, used for poor circumstances or a weak excuse.
phrases.en_equiv: to be poor; to be lame

explain_en: It describes tight finances or a cramped, stuffy space. It is also used for weak, lame words, as in '변명이 옹색하다', which is close to '궁색하다'.

examples.ko: 우리 아버지는 자린고비라서 불을 항상 꺼요.
examples.en: My father is a penny pincher, so he always turns off the lights.

examples.ko: 그 친구는 자린고비 소리를 들어도 신경 안 써요.
examples.en: That friend doesn't care even when called a miser.

examples.ko: 자린고비처럼 아끼기만 하지 말고 가끔은 쓰세요.
examples.en: Don't just save like a miser, spend sometimes.

examples.ko: 자린고비 같은 사장님이 월급을 올려 주실까요?
examples.en: Would a boss who's as tight as a miser raise our pay?

examples.ko: 누가 자린고비 아니랄까 봐 영수증까지 챙기네요.
examples.en: True to being a skinflint, he even keeps the receipt.

examples.ko: 저는 자린고비는 아니지만 아껴 쓰는 편이에요.
examples.en: I'm not a miser, but I tend to be thrifty.

explain: 돈을 너무 아끼는 사람을 놀리듯이 부르는 말이에요. '구두쇠', '짠돌이'와 비슷하고, 가까운 사이에서 농담처럼 쓰는 경우가 많아요.

phrases.en: That boss is famous for being a miser.
phrases.nuance_ko: '자린고비'와 거의 같은 뜻이고, 조금 더 널리 쓰여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Nearly the same meaning and a bit more widely used.

phrases.example: 제 친구는 짠돌이라서 커피도 잘 안 사요.
phrases.en: My friend is stingy, so he rarely even buys coffee.
phrases.nuance_ko: 편한 사이에서 쓰는 말이고, 남자에게 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Casual, used among close people and more often about men.

phrases.en: I saved like a miser and finally bought a house.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람 말고 아끼는 방식을 비유할 때도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Also works as a comparison for how someone saves, not only as a label.

explain_en: It is a teasing name for a person who is too stingy with money. It is similar to '구두쇠' and '짠돌이', and is often used jokingly between people who are close.

examples.en: Salary is paid on the 25th of every month.
The prize money was paid yesterday.
There is money that hasn't been paid yet.

examples.ko: 지급되는 물건은 마음대로 바꿀 수 없어요.
examples.en: You can't change the items that are provided as you like.
You get a text when the money is paid.
It is scheduled to be paid soon.

explain: 돈이나 물건이 주어질 때 써요. 회사나 정부가 주면 '지급하다', 받는 쪽에서 말하면 '지급되다'예요. '월급', '지원금' 같은 말과 같이 나와요.

phrases.en: The company pays salaries to its employees.
phrases.nuance_ko: 주는 쪽이 주어일 때 쓰는 능동형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The active form, used when the giver is the subject.

phrases.en: The support money hasn't been paid yet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 받을 돈이나 물건이 아직 안 왔을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when money or goods you expect have not arrived.

phrases.en: The salary payment day is the 25th.
phrases.nuance_ko: 돈을 주는 날을 말하는 명사예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A noun for the day on which money is paid.

explain_en: Use it when money or goods are handed out. The giver (a company or government) uses '지급하다'; from the receiving side it is '지급되다'. It appears with words like '월급' and '지원금'.

dis.h: given out by the payer: wages, benefits

p.n: 지급 is money handed out by the giver (wages, aid); 지불 is money paid for something owed.
